title: Heat Pump Rebates in Ottawa 2026: Cold-Climate Rules and Up to $7,500
desc: Ottawa heat pump rebates for 2026 under Home Renovation Savings, with cold-climate performance rules, sizing options and the Better Homes Ottawa loan.
badge: Up to $7,500 for an air-source heat pump
lead: Ottawa averages -13.2°C in January and has reached -32.2°C. The program's cold-climate rules are written for weather like this, and they decide which models qualify.
cards_heading: What Home Renovation Savings pays for a heat pump in Ottawa
cards_intro: We re-read the program's heat pump page and its requirements document on October 3, 2026. No home energy assessment is needed for this stream, but a participating HVAC contractor and written pre-approval are.

cards.title: Air-source, electric, oil, propane or wood heat
cards.note: For a cold-climate air-source heat pump replacing electric resistance, oil, propane or wood as the main heat. A 3-ton system pays $3,750 and 6 tons or more reaches the cap.

cards.title: Air-source, Enbridge gas heat
cards.note: For homes primarily heated by an Enbridge gas furnace or boiler. The cap is reached at 4 tons.

cards.title: Ground-source
cards.note: For electric, oil, propane or wood homes. Gas homes get a flat $3,000. The system must be a full installation sized to the home's load.

cards.title: Rented heat pump
cards.note: Rentals are eligible for any primary heating fuel: $500 per ton for air-source, up to $2,000, or a flat $3,000 for ground-source.

cards.title: More than one outdoor unit
cards.amount: Up to three units, one rebate
cards.note: If several outdoor units are needed to heat the whole home, their tons add up and one rebate is paid on the total, for example 3 + 3 tons for $7,500.

cards.title: One rebate, pre-approved
cards.note: One rebate per home. The contractor needs written pre-approval before installing, files the post-installation application within 30 days, and the cheque arrives within 60 days of approval.

cards.title: Better Homes Ottawa loan
cards.amount: Loan repaid on your tax bill
cards.note: Repaid on the property tax bill over 20 years. Excludes gas upgrades. Up to the lesser of $125,000 or 10% of assessed value, over 20 years.

after_cards: The requirements document lists no end date, but the program's other streams close in late 2026, so check the program page before you sign a contract. Pre-approval is mandatory: an installation done first earns nothing.
sections: What cold-climate means in the rules

The heat pump must be on NRCan's cold-climate list and meet minimum ratings: HSPF2 of 6.6 for Region V, SEER2 of 15.2, a coefficient of performance of 1.8 at -15°C and at least 70% of its rated capacity kept at -15°C. It must be variable capacity and have a rated heating capacity of at least 12,000 BTU/h at 8.3°C. The program's own page says cold-climate models are designed to work in temperatures as low as -30°C.

The 2021 Census counts 407,250 households in Ottawa, with 64% owning and 69% in a house type the program accepts. 44% live in homes built before 1981. Gas homes get $500 per ton up to $2,000, while oil, propane, wood and electric resistance homes get $1,250 per ton up to $7,500. Oil homes must remove or empty the tank with a TSSA-registered contractor.

An Ottawa home can keep existing electric resistance or wood heat as a backup, and a gas home can keep its furnace. The backup is not rebated. For oil homes, the oil system must go, but new electric resistance backup is permitted. This matters in a city where the coldest days drop past the heat pump's best range.

The City's Better Homes Ottawa loan is repaid on the property tax bill and excludes gas upgrades. We recorded up to the lesser of $125,000 or 10% of assessed value, over 20 years, with 0% for households under income thresholds. Check the City's page before relying on those terms.

Electric, oil and wood homes must choose NRCan sizing option C (emphasis on heating) or D (sized on the design heating load). Gas and propane homes can also use options A and B. In a cold city, those two lower options leave more of the load to the backup, which is why they are not paid at the higher rate.
claim_steps: Check the model against NRCan's cold-climate list before you sign.
Confirm eligibility on the program's short form and get the list of participating HVAC contractors.
Choose a contractor from that list. Ask for a load calculation and the NRCan sizing tool form for each outdoor unit.
Wait for written pre-approval before any installation starts.
After the install, check that the contractor files the post-installation application within 30 days, with the final itemized invoice and photos.
faq: How cold must a model work?
It must keep at least 70% of rated capacity at -15 degrees Celsius and have a COP of 1.8 there.
Can I keep my old heating as backup?
Yes. Backup is allowed but not rebated.
